title: a completion row reads as a declaration, and its card is read on resolve
scope:
what a completion item carries on the wire — the label details an editor draws on the
row, the `detail` it draws in the panel, the key its documentation is resolved by — what accepting a
method writes, and the card a `Core` class carries of its own. It does not change which items are
offered where, which is [0193](0193.md)'s, or what accepting a type writes, which is [0194](0194.md)'s.
dependsOnText:
[0193](0193.md) for the list, [0194](0194.md) for the follow text, [0117](0117.md)
for the reference card in the registry.

summary.headline: A completion row reads like the declaration; a description is fetched per row
summary.body:
A row in the completion list shows a method as `name(params)` with its return type at the right,
a constant as `NAME = value`, and a class with its namespace in brackets after the name. The
list no longer carries a description for every row: each row carries a small key, and the editor
asks for the description of the one row it is showing, the same text hovering the name shows.
Accepting a method writes its parentheses. Every `Core` class now carries a one-sentence card.
